worked_solution:
Let $u={log}_{2}⁡({x}^{2}).$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\cdot 2x=\frac{2}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\,⟹\,\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{2}\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $2$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $2$ | $4$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{4}\frac{3{log}_{2}⁡({x}^{2})}{\sqrt{2}x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}{\int }_{2}^{4}{log}_{2}⁡({x}^{2})\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}{\int }_{2}^{4}u\cdot \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{2}{\int }_{2}^{4}u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{3\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{2\sqrt{2}}\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{2}{|}_{2}^{4} \\  & =\frac{3\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{4\sqrt{2}}\cdot (16-4) \\  & =\frac{9\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}
$$
